editorial:
You meet Conor, a quiet 12-year-old who is dealing with a lot. His mom is very sick, kids at school pick on him, and his strict grandma is about to move in. One night, a giant tree monster shows up outside his window. Instead of being scary, this monster tells him three stories and promises to come back for a fourth. The monster is loud, wild, and a little funny, but he is really there to help Conor face feelings he has been hiding. The whole movie has a dark fairy-tale feel, with beautiful drawings that come to life on screen. It is sad and magical at the same time, and you will feel pulled into Conor's world.

The acting is strong, especially from the young lead and the voice behind the monster. The special effects look great, and the pacing keeps you interested without rushing. Some scenes are heavy and might be tough for younger kids, but the story handles grief with care. If you enjoy emotional fantasy films, this one is for you. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Conor's mother passes away. The monster's fourth story is actually Conor's own truth: he has been secretly wishing for her suffering to end, and he feels guilty about it. The monster helps him admit this painful feeling out loud. After her death, Conor moves in with his grandma. He finds his mom's old room, now filled with his drawings, and he finally lets himself cry. The monster's job is done, and Conor learns that facing hard truths is part of healing.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves emotional fantasy stories about family and growing up.
